theme.name: Flat funding and move to self-sufficiency
theme.claim: Core council funding is broadly flat in cash terms for the rest of this Parliament, and reform toward local self-sufficiency is needed to give authorities certainty.

text.line: 1.2.1 The funding available to councils to deliver their core services for the rest of this Parliament is broadly flat, in cash terms.

theme.name: Rising parish precepts
theme.claim: The average parish Band D increase of 6.1% in 2016/17 is notably higher than in the previous five years, and with around 8,800 precepting parishes varying widely in size and precept, this justifies applying referendum principles to larger parishes.

text.line: 3.3.1 Since the introduction of council tax referendums in 2012/13, no referendum principles have been set for local precepting authorities such as town and parish councils (“parishes”), although the Government has made it clear that we would keep this under review and take action if necessary.
However, the increase in the average Band D council tax level of 6.1% set by parishes in 2016/17 is notably higher than those in the previous 5 years, as shown in Table 1 below:
Table 1: Average percentage increase in Band D council tax levels set by parishes
There are around 8,800 precepting parishes in England, which vary widely in terms of resident population and precept charge.

theme.name: Revaluation effects outside local control
theme.claim: The 2017 business rates revaluation is revenue neutral nationally but will raise or lower individual authorities' bills depending on their rateable value performance, creating changes in retained income outside their control.

text.line: 3.4.1 The next business rates revaluation takes effect from 1 April 2017.
Revaluation is a revenue neutral exercise so the total rates bill will stay the same at the England level in real terms, after allowing for appeals.

At the local authority level, overall bills will increase or fall depending upon whether rateable values in that area have performed above or below the average for England, after allowing for appeals.
3.4.2 This creates change in the system outside the control of local authorities.
